first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings support reducing onboarding friction. This is better aligned with sustainable growth than promotional pricing, which previously harmed 30-day retention. Verify the onboarding evidence and run a controlled experiment with qualified-revenue and retention guardrails because downstream revenue impact remains uncertain.

mid.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-simplification experiment. The directly relevant archived result increased completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%, addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable growth. SMB signup simplification also lifted activation and qualified revenue, though its slight retention decline and limited segment replication warrant retention and qualified-revenue guardrails. Avoid promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because its known retention harm conflicts with the primary objective.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. Verified evidence shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing current operating declines and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The competitor’s deeper cut and increased churn conversations raise urgency but do not overturn the known evidence that promotional pricing materially reduced retention. Reassess pricing next cycle when targeted retention-oriented options can be verified.
